reads.metrics: PromQL over a window, each series summed up
reads.traces: Traces by service, operation, failure and duration
reads.siem: Signals raised by its rules, by host and severity
reads.alerts: Alert groups, with who is on call
reads.vulnerabilities: Open vulnerabilities, with fixes and affected hosts

ask.title: Ask
ask.description: Answers cite what was read. Every product is read with your own token, so the assistant sees only what you could open there.
ask.noModel: No language model is set up
ask.noModelDetail: Until an admin sets one under Model, questions are refused and nothing is sent anywhere.
ask.noSourcesDetail: An admin allows the products the assistant may read under Sources.
ask.noConnections: You have not connected a product
ask.noConnectionsDetail: Answers are read with your own token for each product. Connect one under Sources; until then, every lookup answers that it is not connected.
ask.emptyDetail: Such as: did anything unusual happen on web-2 yesterday? Which critical vulnerabilities have a fix? What is incident INC-12 about?
ask.question: Ask a question
ask.placeholder: Ask about hosts, services, alerts, signals or incidents
ask.keys: Enter to send · Shift+Enter for a new line
ask.noData: No product returned data for this question
ask.noDataDetail: Nothing in this answer comes from a source. Check the calls on the right: a product may not be connected, or the query found nothing.
ask.uncitedDetail: This part cites no call. Treat it as the model's words, not as data.
ask.sourcesNoneDetail: Every call an answer makes is listed here, with a link to the page where you see the same data.

history.title: History
history.description: Your conversations. Nobody else sees them, admins included. They are deleted {{days}} days after their last question.

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: The products the assistant may read. Admins allow them; each person connects their own token, and every lookup is made with it.
sources.asYou: Each lookup uses your own token for that product, so an answer holds only what you could open there. Create a token with the viewer role in the product, under Settings, API tokens. A token that can manage a product is refused.
sources.connectDetail: Your token for {{product}}. Every lookup in {{product}} is made with it, as you.
sources.step1: Open {{product}} at {{url}}, under Settings, API tokens.
sources.step2: Create a token with the viewer role and an expiry. If you cannot, an admin of that product creates it for you.
sources.step3: Paste it here. It is checked, sealed with the install's key and never shown again.
sources.tokenHint: Starts with oa_ and the product's name.
sources.editDetail: Whether the assistant may read it, and where.
sources.allowDetail: People can connect their tokens and the tools may read it.
sources.apiUrlHint: Where Assistant reads it, such as its service name in the compose network.
sources.webUrlHint: Citations link here. The API address when left empty.
sources.movedTitle: Everyone's tokens for it are dropped
sources.moved: Tokens were given for the old address and are never sent to a new one. People connect again.

model.title: Model
model.description: The language model that writes the answers. Nothing is sent anywhere until an admin sets one.
model.nowhereDetail: No model is set up, so questions are refused. Set one below; a model on your own server, such as Ollama, keeps everything in your network.
model.sentTo: Questions and what the tools read are sent to {{host}}
model.sentToDetail: Every question, the earlier turns of its conversation and everything the tools return for it go to {{url}}.

network.this-host: That is this host, as far as its address tells.
network.private: That is in your network, as far as its address tells.
network.internet: That is a service on the internet: log lines, metrics and findings leave your network, and its provider's terms apply to them.

model.what: What the model gets, and what it can do
model.what1: The question, the earlier turns of the conversation and the results of the tools it calls. Nothing else is sent.
model.what2: Tools that only read: Logs, Metrics, Traces, SIEM, Alerts, Incidents and Vulnerabilities, each with the asking person's own token.
model.what3: What the tools return is passed as data. Instructions in a log line are not followed, and no link the model writes is opened.
model.what4: It cannot change, run, acknowledge or delete anything.
model.formDetail: Prefer a model on your own server. Any server with OpenAI's chat completions and tool calling works.

baseUrlHint.openai: Up to and with /v1: http://ollama:11434/v1 for Ollama, http://vllm:8000/v1 for vLLM.
baseUrlHint.anthropic: https://api.anthropic.com, or a gateway that speaks the same API.

model.apiKeyHint: If the server needs one. Sealed with the install's key, never shown again, and forgotten when the address changes.
model.apiKeyKept: A key is kept. Leave this empty to keep it.
model.retentionDetail: Conversations are deleted {{days}} days after their last question.
model.retentionHint: 1 to 400. Older ones are deleted when you save.

settingsPage.askAnAdmin: Ask an admin of this Assistant.

account.title: Account
account.description: Your profile, password, two-step verification and where you are signed in.

members.title: Members
members.description: Who can sign in to this Assistant, and with which role. Viewers and editors ask and connect their own tokens; admins also set the model, the sources and the retention, and manage members and tokens. Nobody reads another person's conversations.

signin.title: Sign-in
signin.description: Identity providers people can sign in with, such as OpenAsy Identity, Keycloak or Microsoft Entra ID, and which of their groups give which role.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.description: For scripts and CI. Each token has one role and an expiry, and its own conversations and connected products; the secret is shown once.
